SFI (Sundhedsvæsenets Fælles Indberetningssystem) is a healthcare registration and reporting system in Denmark that serves as a critical data source for clinical quality databases. Specifically, it is the system from which nutrition data is extracted to populate and evaluate indicators for the [[akut-kirurgi-databasen|Akut Kirurgi Databasen]] (AKDB) [^src1]. 

The system's operational limitations and the data quality challenges associated with it were highlighted in the 2023 annual report of the AKDB, which is part of the Regionernes Kliniske Kvalitetsudviklingsprogram (RKKP) [^src1]. Regional comments from the five Danish regions pointed out technical and procedural issues within registration systems like SFI and SMR [^src1]. Notably, it was reported that surgery departments in the Central Denmark Region (Region Midtjylland) lacked an established practice for documenting nutrition using the correct codes in SFI [^src1]. This deficiency in coding practice directly compromised the data pulled for the AKDB, specifically affecting the measurement and reporting of indicator 8 [^src1]. These registration and coding challenges are considered central to understanding the operational limitations and clinical relevance of the database's findings [^src1].
